summary: Jacqueline I. Stone works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned degrees from San Francisco State University and UCLA, studying under William R. LaFleur. She served as Professor at Princeton University (1990–2019) and president of SSJR (~1997–1999).

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who completed doctoral studies under Julius Lipner. She has been affiliated with the University of Manchester, including as an Honorary Research Fellow (attested 2026).

Jacques André was a linguist and historian. After studying at the Faculty of Arts of Paris under Jules Marouzeau, he held posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

Jacques Bacot specialized in Tibetology and linguistics, studying at the EPHE under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held posts at the EPHE (including directeur d’études, 1935–1938), the University of Paris (~1936–1958), and presided over the Société Asiatique (1945–1954).

Jacques David Ehni was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren and the University of Tübingen (~1845–1849) before teaching at the Lyceum of Ludwigsburg and the Humboldt-Gymnasium Ulm.

Jacques Gernet was a scholar of sinology, history, and Buddhist studies who studied at Algiers, INALCO, and EPHE. He held posts at EFEO, EPHE/EHESS, the University of Paris, and Collège de France (1975–1992), and co-founded Paris Diderot University.

Jacques Giès was a sinologist and art historian who studied under Flora Blanchon and at Paris-Sorbonne University. He taught at Paris-Sorbonne (1974–1998) and École du Louvre (1998–2008), and served as chief curator and president (2008–2011) of the Guimet Museum.

Jacques Leider is a historian of Southeast Asia and Buddhist studies. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne and INALCO under Denise Bernot and Pierre L. Lamant. His career includes posts at Chulalongkorn University (1995–1999) and the EFEO (from 2001).
Jacques Maritain was a philosopher who studied at the Lycée Henri-IV and the Faculty of Arts of Paris under Henri Bergson (~1901–1904). He later held a post at the University of Chicago (~1948–1956).

Jacques May specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Constantin Régamey (~1950–1957) and served as editor-in-chief of Hōbōgirin (~1962–1981) and professor at the University of Lausanne (~1970–1992).

Jacques Scheuer was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Université catholique de Louvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Madeleine Biardeau, later serving as professor at Université catholique de Louvain (~1976–2007) and teaching at Centre Sèvres.

Jacques van Ginneken was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck. He held appointments at the Catholic University of America (1923) and Radboud University Nijmegen (1923–1945).

Jacques-Albert Cuttat worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, studying at the universities of Bern and Paris. He taught commercial law at Bern (1935), was a philosophy professor at the Sorbonne, and taught at Columbia University.

Jadunath Sarkar was an Indian historian who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He taught at Patna College (1899–1926), Banaras Hindu University, and Ravenshaw College, and served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1926–1928).
Jae-gwon Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Kim completed a PhD at Ryukoku University (finished 2007) and held a post there.
Jagaddhar Zadoo was an Indology scholar who served at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, between 1924 and 1930, and held the position of Superintendent there in 1947.

Jagadish Chandra Chatterji was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Cambridge. He served as Director of the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1911).

Jagannath Upadhyaya was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He was a professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1980–1983) and became the first director of the Rare Buddhist Text Research Project at CIHTS in 1985.

Jagdish Kashyap worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Patna College, BHU, and under Rahul Sankrityayan. He taught at Banaras Hindu University, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and founded and directed the Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

Jaideva Singh was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Swami Lakshman Joo, Srikrishna Harihirlekar, and Nankoo Bhaya Telang. He served as chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and chaired the Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (1973).
